name: Mexico
sources: GDP $261.3bn and 82.8m people (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, 1990; exact prints $261.254bn and 82,820,170). The XI Censo General de Poblacion of March 1990 counted 81.25m, and the gap to the World Bank series is the usual undercount adjustment.

Inflation 26.7% is the Banco de Mexico CPI annual average for 1990 (December-on-December was 29.9%). The Pacto de Solidaridad Economica, the heterodox incomes pact renewed every few months from December 1987, is what had brought it down from 159% in 1987.
interest_rate 34.8%: the average 28-day Cetes yield for 1990. Positive in real terms, which is how the pact was defended.

Tax take 17% of GDP: federal tax revenue proper was about 11% of GDP, and oil rents remitted by Pemex carry the rest of the budget. Investment split 4.5% public and 14% private against gross fixed capital formation near 18.5% of GDP.

Debt 0.50: total external debt about $104bn at end-1990 (World Bank), and net public sector debt around half of GDP after the Brady agreement signed in February 1990 wrote down roughly $7bn of principal. It falls fast from here.
Oil 2.55 mbd: Pemex crude production averaged 2.548 mbd in 1990.
Defence 0.5% of GDP, the lowest of any large state in the roster and a deliberate constitutional posture since 1917, not an oversight. Strength 8 is an army sized for internal order.

MEXICO CROWDS THE UNITED STATES' PATRONAGE BUDGET, AND THE INTEGRATOR SHOULD KNOW IT. Measured on this branch: politics.rs ranks candidates for American patronage by client_score, and with Mexico on the board that ranking runs Saudi Arabia 4.51, Israel 2.39, Mexico 2.20, South Korea 1.89, Brazil 1.76, Spain 1.60, Turkey 1.58, Venezuela 1.47. statecraft.rs caps a patron at 1.0% of GDP in aid with 0.4% to any one client, so the United States funds about two and a half clients in total, ever. Mexico takes the third slot. Kuwait is nowhere on that list, and Kuwait being paid is what lets it ask for a protector before Iraq invades in August 1990.

The test that watches for a great power being dragged into someone else's war requires that to happen in 3 to 11 runs out of 12. It reads 4 on master and 3 on this branch: still inside the band, at its exact floor. It did read 2 - outside the band - until the GDP and population figures in this region were requeried against the World Bank series and corrected, which is a warning rather than a reprieve, because a test that moves between 2 and 4 on a data correction of one or two percent is not measuring what it thinks it is. The next region merged will probably push it under.

authoritarianism 0.52 puts Mexico just under the electoral ceiling, which is the right side of the line: the PRI held real elections on schedule and lost the presidency in 2000, but 1988 had been decided by a computer crash. Stability 55 and separatism 0.04 — Chiapas in 1994 is an insurgency, not a secession, and is not scripted here. No figure in this file was tuned to any test. For Mexico to fall below Kuwait in the patronage ranking its relation with the United States would have to be under 17 on the -100..100 scale, and January 1990 is Salinas at his most pro-American: the Brady agreement signed that February, the GATT joined in 1986, the free trade proposal four months away. The transcribed value is 45, the same as Brazil's. The real finding is that patronage is a global argmax against a fixed budget and so is not roster-invariant: at 190 nations every patron funds the two or three richest oil states on Earth, and every calibration keyed to the ordering of a 25-nation world breaks the same way.

pop_growth_1990 = 2.0225%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series MEX (Mexico): 73,506,846 in 1984 to 81,247,182 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

ALL 48 OF THE 1990-ELIGIBLE TECHNOLOGIES WERE RULED FOR THIS NATION, one at a time, against a standard published per technology rather than per country. 3 were held and are listed below with their citations; 45 were refused. The refused ids are named at the end of this note so that a reader can tell a cell that was examined and refused from a cell nobody looked at - those are different claims and the schema would otherwise flatten them into the same silence.

RULED AND REFUSED, ids only (the reasoning for each refusal is held with the board that wrote it, one standard per technology): core_cmos_submicron, core_packet_internetworking, core_single_mode_fiber, core_carbon_composites, core_combined_cycle_turbine, core_pcr, comp_microprocessor, comp_risc_superscalar, comp_relational_database, comm_fibre_optic_backbone, comm_geostationary_comsat, ener_seismic_3d_imaging, ener_horizontal_drilling, ener_gas_turbine_combined_cycle, ener_crystalline_silicon_module, matl_semiconductor_lithography, matl_composite_structures, matl_industrial_robotics, matl_lean_production, matl_single_crystal_superalloy, matl_rare_earth_magnet, matl_stereolithography, aero_precision_munitions, aero_pulse_doppler_radar, aero_stealth_shaping, aero_quiet_submarine, aero_recon_satellite, bio_recombinant_pharma, bio_universal_immunisation, bio_cross_sectional_imaging, bio_conjugate_vaccine, bio_monoclonal_antibody, bio_automated_sequencing, tran_container_intermodal, tran_post_panamax_ship, tran_electronic_freight_documents, tran_high_speed_rail, agri_drip_irrigation, agri_composite_membrane, agri_conservation_tillage, agri_integrated_pest_management, agri_protected_cultivation, agri_tissue_culture_propagation, agri_marine_aquaculture, agri_flue_gas_desulphurisation.

COLLISION RESOLVED. Two authoring boards ruled the same cell for this nation and disagreed. The tie-break is uniform across the whole roster and is not a preference between authors: the cell belongs to the board that owns the technology's domain in the registry, which for every non-core id is also its id prefix, and which both cross-domain authors published as their own deferral. core_packet_internetworking -> NOT HELD (semiconductors-computing said held, telecom-space said not held; resolved to the board that owns the Communications domain, telecom-space).

granted.source: R3: Mexico's first cellular services opened in 1989 - Iusacell in Mexico City and Monterrey, and Telcel, created the same year, beginning operations in Tijuana - both on analogue networks. World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 63,926 Mexican mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990.

Mexico's first cellular services opened in 1989: Iusacell (founded 1987) launched analogue cellular in Mexico City and Monterrey, and Telcel, created the same year, began operations in Tijuana. World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 63,926 Mexican mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990.

Mexico's Secretaria de Salud ran a national oral rehydration programme through the second half of the 1980s, distributing ORS sachets branded Vida Suero Oral through the public health service alongside a mass social-marketing campaign; the sharp fall in Mexican under-five diarrhoeal mortality that followed is a standard case study in the child-survival literature. FLAGGED: the programme is real and well documented but I could not fix its launch year to a single date this session, so the cell is dated only to 'the second half of the 1980s'. Note that Mexico is refused bio_universal_immunisation on DTP3 53, so this is a nation whose ORT programme outran its immunisation programme — which is the actual 1990 Mexican picture.
